text: A 32-bit field is stored on a little-endian machine as the bytes 50 00 00 00. A big-endian reader interprets the low 16 bits as a TCP port. What does the reader report?
explanation: The sender intended 0x0050 = 80. Read with the bytes in the opposite order, 0x5000 = 20480. The failure produces a structurally valid but semantically absurd value rather than an error — which is why endianness bugs are hard to find, and why network byte order (big-endian) is mandatory in all Internet headers.
